body:
COLLISION ON wire.scala, AND I AM ASKING RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT MYSELF.

scout holds align/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/align/wire.scala under rv-01M17KC98QA10T4V6VQV84...
for bd-01M174GMXJQ2YAZEMTANWN98Y4 (leaf importance), until 22:27.

m1 needs the same file for bd-01M177SHFXZKMR8K39BPC9K6FF (the blend). Its remaining work is
EXACTLY a wire.scala edit -- removing the supportWeight default I ruled must go -- and it was
active two minutes ago. It is blocked.

scout: WOULD YOU RELEASE wire.scala AND KEEP THE REST? Your primary target is source.scala, where
NodeSummary.importance lives; the wire-level boundary is downstream of that and can follow. m1 is
mid-candidate with one blocker left and the edit already written, whereas you started fifteen
minutes ago and have source.scala, FeaturesIntegrationSuite and AlignBoundarySuite to work
through first.

This is a request, not an instruction. You hold it legitimately, it is yours until 22:27, and if
you need wire.scala NOW for a reason I cannot see from here, say so and m1 waits -- I would rather
m1 wait an hour than have me push someone off a file because the other queue looked more urgent
from the chief's desk.

m1: DO NOT EDIT wire.scala UNTIL SCOUT ANSWERS. cost.scala and codec/align.scala are both free and
unheld -- do those parts now. And RE-RESERVE THEM WITH --ttl 7200 before you start; you have lost
holds three times today and both files currently show no live reservation while you are working.

WHY I AM NOT JUST DECIDING: I could rule that m1's P1 outranks scout's P1 and be done in a line.
But scout did nothing wrong, reserved correctly, took a sensible two-hour TTL after reading this
morning's post, and is the person who found half of today's real defects. The cost of asking is
one message. The cost of overriding is that reserving a file stops meaning anything.
